CS3-H-01.note: Ages 'fall in no order' and highest bench younger than two below it refutes an ordered sequence; 'coeval' would be refuted by any age spread, not by disorder specifically.

CS3-H-02.note: 'crews were sent on nothing more' demands sufficiency, which only 'dispositive' carries; 'premonitory' and 'ubiquitous' both describe the correction, not the old belief.

CS3-H-03.note: 'vernacular' is defensible: the refutation opposes scribal/native hands to classical inscriptional geometry, and 'the letters his hand already knew' reads as the vernacular hand as easily as as derivation.

CS3-H-04.note: 'recorded ______ rather than a system' fixes the antonym; accumulation is the only option that opposes 'system'. Exaggeration/abbreviation/facsimile are not live at all.

CS3-H-05.note: 'not only where the food went but whether it was watched' = the memory account is insufficient, not false, so 'unwarranted'/'premature' overshoot.

CS3-H-06.note: 'a sequence no primate performs and no account of the ecology predicts' is peculiarity, not ambiguity; 'equivocal' is the only near miss.

CS3-H-07.note: 'seniors save it for the years in which nothing else will do' plus a cost of exercise supports 'discretionary' nearly as well as 'latent'; the disambiguator is only that 'in practice' contrasts a live right with a dormant one. Genuinely close.

CS3-H-08.note: Eighteen wet years mistaken for the long-run norm; 'generous' inverts the error the negotiators made.

CS3-H-09.note: A is live blind (a third sentence resolving a gap named in the second is a common shape) and only the text rules it out.

CS3-H-10.note: A is a strong near-miss but is false on one word: the text allows the four-fifths cost saving rather than disputing it.

CS3-H-11.note: Wild hooks come from stems 'already curved', so the natural behavior resembles the feat without supplying the bending.

CS3-H-12.note: For a 'function of the second sentence' stem, 'concedes a limit on the instrument the first sentence introduces' is the default-legal option; A/C/D are all either forward-referring or extreme, so the option set alone gets there.

CS3-H-13.note: A and C are extreme ('questions whether at all', 'cannot be accounted for'), B mislocates a measurement; the neutral descriptive option wins without the passage.

CS3-H-14.note: Restrict-rather-than-withdraw is the uniquely hedged option in a set where the other three are absolutes; blind-pickable.

CS3-H-15.note: C ('endorses the older answer') is legal blind; only the text shows both results were reported and neither alone carried the conclusion.

CS3-H-16.note: C is close and arguably true: the sentence does concede an error that was understandable. A wins only because 'not simple ignorance' plus 'a rule nobody can administer is not a rule' is an affirmative defense, not a concession. Defensible either way.

CS3-H-17.note: B is not false of Text 2: the only mechanism it names is melt-smoothing, and thirty-years-warm/none-cold implies the whole eleven comes from there. A wins on responsiveness (the uneven distribution is the point) rather than on truth, which makes B genuinely defensible.

CS3-H-18.note: D is excluded by 'nine states now allow'; C restates the closing sentence.

CS3-H-19.note: A is the exact mirror trap; Text 2's whole move is 'that is not the same schedule... it is two different lives'.

CS3-H-20.note: 'its time course is about as described' kills A; the two-or-three vs twenty words per minute contrast is the argument for D.

CS3-H-21.note: The fully-roaded control valleys make the observation-effort account the response; Text 2 never contests the rainfall trend.

CS3-H-22.note: 'The two accounts predict the same re-hiding' explicitly accepts the behavior; the punishment history replaces projection.

CS3-H-23.note: 'The flexibility is real. It is also the same property that...' rules out A and B; C invents a remedy the text never proposes.

CS3-H-24.note: C is the strongest trap but is refuted by 'it is the italic's economy' - Text 2 keeps the credit with the type, just not with the slope.
